builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Low-Latency MoE Inference in Space Data Centers: A Wireless-Power-Transfer Perspective
summary: The method replaces passive, per-satellite solar power allocation in orbital data centers with laser-based wireless power transfer that redistributes harvested energy from idle to active MoE experts, controlled by a two-sided water-filling policy. It costs inter-satellite WPT hardware, incurs transfer losses, and adds a power-routing control layer, with benefits bounded by link efficiency and formation geometry. It can fail or yield no gain when WPT efficiency is low, expert activation is balanced, or the infrastructure does not exist.
rationale: The technique assumes space-based data centers with satellite power-transfer hardware, which is entirely outside the infrastructure and production scope of an ML engineer with one GPU or API access.
technique: Inter-satellite wireless power transfer for MoE inference

claims.statement: The method replaces passive, per-satellite solar power allocation in orbital data centers with laser-based wireless power transfer that redistributes harvested energy from idle to active MoE experts, controlled by a two-sided water-filling policy. It costs inter-satellite WPT hardware, incurs transfer losses, and adds a power-routing control layer, with benefits bounded by link efficiency and formation geometry. It can fail or yield no gain when WPT efficiency is low, expert activation is balanced, or the infrastructure does not exist.

Simulations with Mixtral-8x7B and Phi-3.5-MoE show up to 29.25% lower inference latency than without WPT (a latency factor of about 1.41x), with gains depending on formation compactness and transfer efficiency.
